name: Kairox Systems
long_description:
Kairox Systems combines the speed of aerial drones and the stealth of underwater drones into one vehicle. We can look for mines in a strait, fly out of the water to inspect a coastline, and then engage maritime threats in one go. 

Joel, Alex, and Jorge all met at MIT. After conversations with warfighters and drone researchers, they decided to create a vehicle unlike any before: A long-range vehicle that is truly amphibious, low-cost enough for one-way swarms, can operate fully autonomously, and can be repurposed on the front lines. Engaged with the Marine Corps and validated with end users across the U.S. and allied militaries.

launches.title: Kairox Systems: Drones that can fly and swim
launches.tagline: Autonomous drones that fly and swim
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Tempest is an autonomous fixed-wing drone that flies, dives below the surface, swims, and flies back out. Missions that need two drones today will need only one. If you have any connections in the DoW, contact [joel@kairoxsys.com](mailto:joel@kairoxsys.com).

<https://youtu.be/bRnMZDK8ZvY>

**The problem:**

Amphibious operations across the world rely on unmanned systems. After talking to Navy officers, SOF operators, and researchers at MIT's Marine Robotics Group, we kept hearing the same thing: air and sea missions need separate drones, separate operators, and separate logistics.

**Our solution:**

Our flagship drone, Tempest, pairs the speed and range of an aerial drone with the stealth of an underwater drone. Tempest is a VTOL fixed-wing drone with a pressure vessel at its core, capable of autonomous navigation across both domains.

**Where we are:**

Tempest is currently undergoing rigorous testing of its multi-domain transitions. We have validated the concept with end users across the U.S. and allied militaries and are building toward procurement.

**The team:**

* **Joel Santiago-Baretti (CEO):** MIT Mechanical Engineering. Previously founded a startup that built ruggedized edge-compute devices for combat medics. Published in IEEE OCEANS.
* **Alex Rice (CTO):** MIT Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. Previously at MITRE, NASA, MIT Lincoln Lab, and Draper. Published in IEEE OCEANS.
* **Jorge Cavazos (COO):** MIT Aerospace Engineering. Previously the lead ADCS (attitude control) engineer at Oligo Space, where he owned everything from control laws to hardware-in-the-loop qualification.

**Our ask:**

* **Are you in the defense or maritime world?** We'd love intros to program offices, special operators, and maritime security teams in the U.S. and allied militaries.
* **Investors:** [Book a time with us](https://yc.link/cal/UerQD5MzPN).
